nodes.label: Statutes, Authorities and Statutory Framework
nodes.summary: Key Hong Kong ordinances governing trusts: Trustee Ordinance, Perpetuities and Accumulations Ordinance, Conveyancing and Property Ordinance, and the regulatory framework for charities.

nodes.label: Trustee Ordinance (Cap 29) Overview
nodes.summary: The Trustee Ordinance (Cap 29) is the primary statute governing trustees in Hong Kong. It provides for trustee powers, duties, investment, delegation, maintenance, advancement, and the statutory duty of care.

nodes.label: Trustee Powers Under Cap 29
nodes.summary: The Trustee Ordinance confers powers of sale, insurance, receipt, delegation, and the power to employ agents. These powers supplement the trust instrument and may be excluded or modified.

nodes.label: Trustee Investment Under Cap 29 s.4
nodes.summary: Trustees may invest trust funds in any type of investment as if they were the absolute beneficial owner, subject to the standard investment criteria and the duty to take advice (Cap 29 s.4).

nodes.label: Statutory Duty of Care Under Cap 29 s.41W
nodes.summary: The Trustee Ordinance imposes a statutory duty of care on trustees: such care and skill as is reasonable in the circumstances, having regard to any special knowledge or experience of the trustee (s.41W).

nodes.label: Maintenance and Advancement Under Cap 29 s.27
nodes.summary: Trustees may apply capital for the advancement or benefit of a beneficiary before their interest vests, subject to the trustee's discretion and the terms of the trust (Cap 29 s.27).

nodes.label: Perpetuities and Accumulations (Cap 2)
nodes.summary: The Perpetuities and Accumulations Ordinance (Cap 2) governs the rule against perpetuities and accumulations in HK. Trusts must not exceed the perpetuity period (generally 80 years or a life in being plus 21 years).

nodes.label: Conveyancing and Property Ordinance (Cap 219) Formalities
nodes.summary: Cap 219 s.5 requires declarations of trust of land to be evidenced in writing signed by the person able to declare the trust. Dispositions of equitable interests must also be in writing (s.5(2)).

nodes.label: Charities Regulation in HK
nodes.summary: Charitable trusts and institutions in HK are regulated by the Inland Revenue Ordinance (charitable exemption), the Companies Ordinance (charitable companies), and common law. HK does not have a dedicated Charities Act but follows the Pemsel heads.
